faq.q: How is the redness index computed?
faq.a: At each capture the app finds the face landmarks, separates the skin and splits it into five zones. Each skin pixel's colour is converted to CIELAB, where the a* axis measures redness. A zone's redness index is the median a* of that zone minus the median a* of all the skin in the same photo: a positive number means the zone is redder than the rest of your own skin. It is a relative measure for tracking over time, with no disease threshold.
No. It is a personal diary: no severity thresholds, no "skin health" score, and it does not replace a dermatologist.

faq.q: Where are my photos stored, and who can see them?
faq.a: Photos and readings live on Supabase (servers in Sydney, Australia) in a private store. Row-level security lets only your own account read or write them, and photos open only through short-lived signed links. Nothing is shared, sold or used to train models; Delete account removes everything immediately.
No. SkinSense is a graduation project: free, no ads, no paid plan.

faq.q: Which devices does it work on?
faq.a: Web: Chrome or Edge on a desktop or laptop with a webcam. Android: phones on Android 7.0 or newer with an arm64 chip, installed from the APK file. Phone browsers and iPhone are not supported yet.

Privacy.title: Privacy policy
Privacy.updated: Updated 13 Sep 2026 · Graduation project, free of charge
Privacy.intro: SkinSense is a personal skin diary. What you create is shown only to you, on your own account. This page lists exactly what the app stores and why.

sections.title: What is stored
body: Your Google account: the email, name and avatar Google returns when you sign in. Used only to recognise you when you come back; there is no separate password.
The face photos you take in the app, with the time taken, brightness and whether white balance was locked.
Spots you tap on a photo yourself: their position on the face and the matching skin zone.
Per-zone readings (forehead, both cheeks, nose, chin): redness, unevenness and pixel count, computed at capture time. The face landmarks and skin mask used to compute them are not kept.
Your evening routine: the steps you define and which ones you ticked each night.
A session cookie in the browser so you do not have to sign in every visit.

sections.title: How it is used
body: Only to show you your diary, readings and trends. Nothing is shared, sold, used for ads, behavioural analytics or model training.
The app does not diagnose. Readings are relative measurements on your own photos, not medical conclusions.

sections.title: Where it lives
body: The database and photos are on Supabase (servers in Sydney, Australia). Every table has row-level security: only the account that created a row can read or write it.
Photos sit in a private bucket with no public URL; the app opens them through short-lived signed links for the owner only.
The website runs on Vercel. The Android app talks directly to Supabase.

sections.title: Deleting your data
body: The “Delete account” button in the app immediately removes every photo, spot, reading, routine and the account itself. No copy is kept and it cannot be undone.
You can also revoke SkinSense's access in your Google account's security settings.
